latest_release.name: Release 4.15.1
latest_release.body:
This a maintenance release hosting a lot of bug fixes and bringing pwntools to the latest Python versions. It contains a long overdue relaxation of the [Unicorn Engine](https://github.com/unicorn-engine/unicorn) version dependency to allow easy installation on Python 3.14+. Many fixes targetted the latest development branch originally and were only backported to the 4.15.* release later to include them in a patch release earlier. Thank you to everyone helping with this release!

## What's Changed
* Allow running with Unicorn 2.1.[34] but throw when emulating MIPS by @peace-maker in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2721
* Support paginated libc.rip API requests by @peace-maker in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2767
* Support `context.timeout` in ~/.pwn.conf by @Feyorsh in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2592
* fix: pad bytes fields to correct field size in FileStructure by @nightcityblade in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2694
* Fix _build_date() crash on non-standard locale date strings by @coder999999999 in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2701
* fix: apply force_to_bytes to readline result in non-term_mode path by @danstam in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2707
* ROP: fix `ROP(ELF(exe)).leave` is `None` in some ELF by @RocketMaDev in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2506
* checksec: more forgiving when passed directory arguments by @tesuji in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2530
* Raise EOFError during process.recv when stdout closes on Windows by @peace-maker in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2524
* Fix a bug that incorrectly reports GNU_STACK missing when its not. by @devx00 in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2493
* Fix aarch64 ABI by @k4lizen in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2598
* Fix `log.progress` ignoring `context.log_console` by @peace-maker in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2610
* GitHub Actions: Test on Python 3.14 by @cclauss in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2627
* safeeval: allow LIST_APPEND and SET_ADD opcodes (Python 3.14) by @ChrisJr404 in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2722
* Add aarch64_be qemu mapping by @OBarronCS in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2653
* Remove "pip" as explicit dependency by @peace-maker in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2642
* fix(libcdb-cli): return early if no matched libc found by @the-soloist in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2646
* asm: try native binutils before fallback architectures by @peace-maker in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2669
* Fix `tty` and `raw` arguments in ssh.process by @peace-maker in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2699
* Close SSH client connection when authentication failed by @peace-maker in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2688
* refactor: replace unsafe eval with ast.literal_eval in ROP cache loading by @RinZ27 in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2677
* fix(dirent): allow bytes with trailing 0 when parsing dirents by @RocketMaDev in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2803
* fix(elf): prevent elf.libc returning the executable when its name starts with libc[.-] by @h4kk4p4kk4 in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2781
* ssh: Discard stderr of `lsb_release` for Distro lookup by @peace-maker in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2704
* fix(packing): dd() raises TypeError on a bytearray destination by @MaxFreedomPollard in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2772
* gdb.corefile: Run gdb directly to prevent detach race by @peace-maker in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2787
* fix(srop): correct amd64 SigreturnFrame uc_sigmask offset by @tarann26 in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2762
* fix pwnlib.shellcraft submodule imports on python 3.12+ by @clmoon2 in https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/pull/2739
* fix(regsort)

# pwntools - CTF toolkit
![pwntools logo](https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/blob/stable/docs/source/logo.png?raw=true)

[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/pwntools?style=flat)](https://pypi.python.org/pypi/pwntools/)
[![Docs](https://readthedocs.org/projects/pwntools/badge/?version=stable)](https://docs.pwntools.com/)
[![GitHub Workflow Status (dev)](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/Gallopsled/pwntools/ci.yml?branch=dev&logo=GitHub)](https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Adev)
[![Coveralls](https://img.shields.io/coveralls/github/Gallopsled/pwntools/dev?logo=coveralls)](https://coveralls.io/github/Gallopsled/pwntools?branch=dev)
[![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg?style=flat)](http://choosealicense.com/licenses/mit/)
[![Packaging status](https://img.shields.io/repology/repositories/python:pwntools)](https://repology.org/project/python:pwntools/versions)
[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/809590285687980052?label=Discord&style=plastic)](https://discord.gg/96VA2zvjCB)
[![Twitter](https://img.shields.io/twitter/follow/Pwntools)](https://twitter.com/pwntools)

Pwntools is a CTF framework and exploit development library. Written in Python, it is designed for rapid prototyping and development, and intended to make exploit writing as simple as possible.

```python
from pwn import *
context(arch = 'i386', os = 'linux')

r = remote('exploitme.example.com', 31337)
# EXPLOIT CODE GOES HERE
r.send(asm(shellcraft.sh()))
r.interactive()
```

# Documentation

Our documentation is available at [docs.pwntools.com](https://docs.pwntools.com/)

A series of tutorials is also [available online](https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools-tutorial#readme)

To get you started, we've provided some example solutions for past CTF challenges in our [write-ups repository](https://github.com/Gallopsled/pwntools-write-ups).

# Installation

Pwntools is best supported on 64-bit Ubuntu LTS releases (22.04 and 24.04).  Most functionality should work on any Posix-like distribution (Debian, Arch, FreeBSD, OSX, etc.).  

Pwntools supports Python 3.10+ since version 5.0.0.  Use Pwntools 4.x for older versions as well as Python 2.7. Most of the functionality of pwntools is self-contained and Python-only.  You should be able to get running quickly with

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install python3 python3-pip python3-dev git libssl-dev libffi-dev build-essential
python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip
python3 -m pip install --upgrade pwntools
```


However, some of the features (assembling/disassembling foreign architectures) require non-Python dependencies.  For more information, see the [complete installation instructions here](https://docs.pwntools.com/en/stable/install.html).
